payload.title: auditor-tier1-probe.sh is invocation-mutating: any double-run within a tick silently downgrades SPAWN to DEBOUNCED
payload.summary: scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh performs a read-modify-write of docs/data/auditor-tier1-spawn-debounce.json inside _spawn_debounce_decision() on EVERY invocation. The script is therefore not idempotent: calling it twice in one cron tick consumes the spawn slot on run 1 and returns DEBOUNCED on run 2. The downgrade is one-directional (SPAWN to DEBOUNCED, never the reverse), so a careless re-run can only ever SUPPRESS a legitimate audit, never cause a spurious one. Failure is silent - both runs emit well-formed JSON and nothing marks the second as a re-derivation.

evidence.write_path: _spawn_debounce_decision() at :910, ledger mutation at :931-940 (last_spawn_at, spawn_count+1, window_expires_at)
evidence.live_reproduction: 2026-08-25T01:00Z tick. Run 1 at 01:21:47Z gave spawn_decision=SPAWN and stamped the ledger last_spawn_at=2026-08-25T01:21:47Z spawn_count=8 window_expires_at=2026-08-25T02:21:47Z. Run 2 at 01:23:02Z, same tick, same signature, gave spawn_decision=DEBOUNCED. Only last_seen_at moved; the ledger itself stayed correct.

payload.why_it_matters: The tier-1 cron prompt explicitly instructs the caller to read spawn_decision from THIS tick own JSON directly and NOT to re-derive it. That instruction is currently the ONLY thing standing between a re-run and a suppressed audit - the safety lives in prose in a cron prompt, not in the script. The same prompt carries a deliberate fail-open clause for a missing or unparseable spawn_decision, which shows the design intent is that a read fault must never silently suppress. An invocation-mutating probe defeats that intent through a different door: the decision is not missing, it is silently WRONG.
payload.contributing_factor: The probe conflates two jobs in one entrypoint - emitting a health verdict (naturally idempotent, safe to call for any reason: debugging, shape-checking, piping to jq) and consuming a rate-limit token (inherently single-shot). Anyone who treats it as the former corrupts the latter.
payload.proposed_remedy: Split the two jobs. Options in order of preference: (a) add a --decide flag so the ledger write happens only under --decide, making the bare invocation a pure read; (b) have callers READ docs/data/auditor-tier1-last-trigger.json, which the probe already writes with the full verdict, rather than re-invoking; (c) make the ledger write idempotent per fire_tick by keying the entry on (signature, fire_tick) so a second run in the same tick is a no-op rather than a downgrade. Option (c) is the most robust because it fixes the hazard even for callers who never read the docs.
payload.do_not: Do NOT address this by re-arming com.vn-market.fleet-push or by adding or retargeting an ack-ledger entry for it - both are explicitly FORBIDDEN by task_board.ready.106 status_note. This row is about the probe entrypoint contract only, NOT about the fleet-push signature that happened to expose it.

related_rows.ready.106: FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-PROBE-SCORES-DELIBERATELY-DISABLED-LAUNCHD-JOB-AS-DEGRADED owns the fleet-push FALSE POSITIVE that generated the signature. Different defect, same script. Currently dispatch_lane=null so it is unpickable.

payload.dedup_note: Matched by SUBJECT against the hot board and docs/data/orch/archive/2026-08.json before filing. ready.106 and backlog.506 both touch this script or its ledger but neither is about the entrypoint idempotency contract. No existing row covers this.
payload.self_disclosure: The router itself caused the double-invocation, by re-running the probe to get clean JSON after a tail filter truncated the first output. The tick was NOT suppressed - run 1 SPAWN was correctly treated as authoritative per the cron prompt, and the system-auditor was spawned. Filed so the next caller is not so lucky.
